LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we construct sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the subject and the verb in sentences

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. affirm the importance of subject-verb agreement in sentences.  Read texts on varied topics such as outdoor games and identify the subject and verbs in the sentences. Learners who may not turn pages to use page-turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Brainstorm and make short notes on the relationship between a subject and a verb in a sentence in terms of number and person, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Read sentences and label How do we construct sentences? 140 subject-verb agreement in them,  Make sentences based on outdoor sports in which the rule of subject-verb agreement has been applied,  Share the sentences in charts for peer review.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject-Verb Agreement together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration is enhanced by the learner recognising the value of others ideas when sharing sentences on charts for peer review.

Values:
Love is enhanced as the learner shows a caring attitude while peer reviewing peers’ sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Value for sports is enhanced as the learner reads texts on varied topics such outdoor games.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of subject-verb agreement when editing their written work in subjects such as Integrated Science

and Pre-Technical Studies.
